questions.prompt: Right after a fresh install, can you connect with the `sa` login?
options: Yes, `sa` has a default password you can look up
Yes, `sa` is enabled whenever Windows Authentication is
No, `sa` doesn't exist on Express editions
No, installs default to Windows Authentication only; `sa` stays disabled until you enable Mixed Mode and set its password
questions.explanation: There is no default SQL username/password waiting for you. Your Windows account is added as `sysadmin`, and `sa` exists only as a disabled account name.

questions.prompt: Which system database is the template for every new database you create?
questions.explanation: `model` is the template. `master` tracks server-wide config and logins, `msdb` is used by SQL Server Agent, and `tempdb` is scratch space rebuilt on every restart.

source.section: 1. What You Get When You Install SQL Server

questions.prompt: SQL Server is installed as the named instance `SQLEXPRESS` on your machine. Which server name connects to it from SSMS?
questions.explanation: A named instance is accessed as `.\SQLEXPRESS` (or `localhost\SQLEXPRESS`, `MACHINE\SQLEXPRESS`). Just `.` or `localhost` reaches the default instance `MSSQLSERVER`.

source.section: 1. What You Get When You Install SQL Server

questions.prompt: Put the steps for creating a dedicated SQL login for your API in order.
steps: Enable Mixed Mode authentication in the server properties and restart the SQL Server service
Create the login with `CREATE LOGIN AppUser WITH PASSWORD = ...`
In the app's database, run `CREATE USER AppUser FOR LOGIN AppUser` and add it to `db_datareader` / `db_datawriter`
Reconnect in SSMS with SQL Server Authentication to test the login
questions.explanation: SQL logins need Mixed Mode first. A login alone can't touch any database, so it must be mapped to a database user with least-privilege roles before testing.

source.section: 3. How to Create a Server Login to Use

questions.prompt: You can already connect with Windows Authentication. Why might your ASP.NET Core API still need a SQL login?
options: Windows Authentication is slower for queries
SQL logins bypass all permission checks
The API is a background process that needs its own identity, and once it runs where Windows Auth doesn't reach, it needs a SQL login
EF Core can't use Windows Authentication at all
questions.explanation: Windows Auth works for the app only while it runs under an account SQL Server trusts on the same domain or machine. Elsewhere, an app service account uses SQL Server Authentication.
